newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING Global Fund returns up 31.7 percent.
newsitem.headline: ING Global Fund returns up 31.7 percent.

text.p: ING said on Monday its ING Bank Global Fund had boosted net asset value per share by 31.7 percent over the financial year ended September 30, 1996, after adjustment for dividend.
Invested capital mushroomed 170 percent to 119.1 million guilders, reflecting an increase in the number of shares outstanding as well as a growth in net asset value, ING said.
As such the ING Global Fund topped the 12-month performance rankings of Amsterdam-listed worldwide equity funds compiled by Rabobank's IRIS research arm to end-October, ING said in a statement.
The ING Global Fund invested in Austria, Greece, Portugal, Croatia and Hungary for the first time and built up some small positions in Latin America.
The percentage invested in Dutch securities remained stable at 29 percent of fund equity, while U.S. investments were slightly increased to 28 percent.
Japanese investments were reduced slightly to 15 percent, while investments in the rest of the Far East were reduced to some six percent.
The fund said it was reasonably optimistic of an average annual world economic growth rate of two to three percent, while inflation and interest rates were likely to remain low.
Earnings growth would slow, but remain at a reasonable level.
As such world stock markets were likely to continue their upward climb in the coming period, albeit at a slower rate, ING predicted.
The fund is proposing a stock dividend of two percent, to be paid from the tax-free share premium reserve.
